definition.def: If you have sympathy for someone who is in a bad situation, you are sorry for them, and show this in the way you behave towards them.
examples: We expressed our sympathy for her loss.
I have had very little help from doctors and no sympathy whatsoever.
I wanted to express my sympathies on your resignation.

definition.def: If you have sympathy with someone's ideas or opinions, you agree with them.
examples: I have some sympathy with this point of view. [+ with]
Lithuania still commands considerable international sympathy for its cause. [+ for]

definition.def: If you take some action in sympathy with someone else, you do it in order to show that you support them.
examples: Several hundred workers struck in sympathy with their colleagues.
Milne resigned in sympathy because of the way Donald had been treated.

examples.sentence: He has even-handed sympathy for both the fugitive king and the fierce republican regime that hunted him, and he succeeds in his desire to explore far more of the background of the story than previous books on the subject have done.
The person who deserves most sympathy is the French astronomer Guillaume Le Gentil.
James Petherick, who plays the hero, fails to gain the sympathy of the audience, who should be moved by the ups and downs in his life.
